papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Induces Glial Dysfunction, Synaptic Loss, Metabolic Imbalance, and Cognitive Impairment in 12-Month-Old Mice: Protective Effects of D30.
papers.summary: In 12-month-old mice, long-term sleep deprivation (LSD) caused sustained reductions in dendritic spine density, synaptic protein levels, and microglial/astrocytic morphological complexity, along with disrupted mitochondrial metabolism involving the TCA cycle, AMPK signaling, and lipid homeostasis. Treatment with D30 ameliorated these deficits, preserving glial homeostasis, restoring synaptic protein expression and spine density, rebalancing systemic metabolism, and improving cognitive performance.

papers.title: Editorial: Criticality: a novel brain metric associated with sleep that may elucidate sleep's influence on adolescent depression.
papers.journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
papers.summary: This editorial proposes brain criticality, an EEG measure of neural dynamics and information processing capacity, as a novel mechanistic lens linking sleep disturbance to adolescent depression. It outlines how depression-related deviations from criticality could reflect a shifted set point, altered drift, or failed reset, each predicting distinct clinical presentations, and highlights the immediate translational potential of criticality metrics from existing EEG data.

papers.title: Tau-associated neuronal loss in the intermediate nucleus of the human hypothalamus, a putative VLPO analog, in progressive supranuclear palsy and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This postmortem study examined neuronal loss and tau pathology in the intermediate nucleus (IntN) of the hypothalamus in progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). They found profound IntN degeneration in PSP (84% neuron reduction) and progressive loss of galanin-positive neurons in higher AD stages, suggesting disease-specific vulnerability consistent with sleep phenotype differences.

papers.title: Fast-ripples are emergent properties of neuronal networks
papers.summary: Combining in silico simulations, neuronal cultures, rodent epilepsy models, and human microwire recordings, this study found that most fast-ripples (250-500 Hz) reflect stochastic network activity rather than distinctly generated pathological entities. Fast-ripple incidence exceeded chance in awake rodents and humans but not in neuronal cultures or sleeping rodents, suggesting their higher prevalence in epileptogenic tissue is primarily due to increased excitation and/or neural synchronization.

papers.title: Mapping and modulating brain dynamics in aging and neurodegeneration with electroencephalography and integrated neurotechnologies in primates.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes EEG methodologies in non-human primates (NHPs), highlighting their value as a translational platform for studying aging and neurodegeneration. It summarizes EEG signatures in normal aging and disease models, and discusses integration with other modalities and neuromodulation techniques to test causality and translate findings to humans.

papers.title: Brain network dynamics in the wake-sleep transition reorganize according to task engagement.
papers.summary: Using EEG-fMRI in individuals fluctuating between alert and drowsy states during active or passive auditory tasks, this study found that actively maintaining task engagement during decreasing alertness increased long-range frontoparietal synchronization and auditory cortex synchronization, while passive listening led to increased parietal and thalamocortical synchronization. The results suggest flexible functional reorganization when alertness declines but cognitive processes persist.

papers.title: Proteoform plasticity modulates the temperature response in circadian timekeeping
papers.summary: Using the Neurospora crassa circadian clock repressor FREQUENCY (FRQ), this study biophysically characterized an isoform-specific intrinsically disordered region (IDR) and identified motifs and molecular behaviors that regulate clock robustness in a temperature-dependent manner. Comparing interactomes of two FRQ isoforms revealed distinct functions and interacting proteins contributing to temperature regulation, highlighting that isoform-specific IDRs enhance and expand clock function context-dependently.

papers.title: Sleep homeostasis in OSA: a complementary neurophysiological outcome measure.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
papers.summary: This article discusses sleep homeostasis in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) as a potential complementary neurophysiological outcome measure, but the abstract was not provided. The journal is the Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine.

papers.title: Early-life environmental enrichment reduces anxiety and induces sex-dependent neuroplasticity in hypothalamic oxytocin and vasopressin neurons.
papers.summary: This study investigated whether perinatal environmental enrichment (PEE) induces persistent behavioral, structural, and neurochemical changes in hypothalamic oxytocin (OXT) and vasopressin (AVP) neurons in male and female mice. PEE reduced anxiety-like behavior, particularly in males, and was accompanied by reduced soma and nuclear size of AVP neurons in PEE males and increased nuclear size and OXT immunoreactivity in both sexes, suggesting long-lasting, sex-dependent neuroplasticity.

papers.title: Reduced sensorimotor lactate concentration and improved sleep efficiency following resistance training in older adults.
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of 12 weeks of explosive lower-body resistance training on sensorimotor lactate and N-acetylaspartate levels, sleep architecture, and sleep quality in older adults. Resistance training significantly reduced resting lactate concentration, improved objective sleep efficiency, and prolonged total sleep time compared to a control group, suggesting benefits for sleep and neural oxidative metabolism.

papers.title: Environmental Enrichment Enhances Visual Function in Adult Amblyopia: Association With miR-132/HDAC3 Regulation.
papers.summary: In an adult amblyopic mouse model, environmental enrichment improved visual function (increased flash visual evoked potential amplitude) and upregulated miR-132 while downregulating HDAC3 in the primary visual cortex; in vitro, miR-132 directly targeted HDAC3 and promoted structural remodeling of cortical neurons.

papers.title: Reactivating a Relaxation Exercise During Sleep to Influence Cortical Hyperarousal in Individuals With Frequent Nightmares.
papers.summary: In individuals with frequent nightmares, reactivating a relaxation-associated odor cue during sleep did not reduce cortical hyperarousal (beta/gamma power) or nightmare symptoms, but unexpectedly reduced spindle count and density. Spindle count correlated positively with subjective wake-after-sleep-onset.

papers.title: EEG Reactivity and Etiology as Prognostic Modifiers in Alpha and Theta Coma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of alpha/theta coma found that overall mortality was 74% and severe disability or death occurred in 83.7%, but EEG reactivity was associated with lower mortality (OR 5.67 for nonreactive) and higher odds of favorable outcome (OR 8.68 for reactive), while etiology (toxic/metabolic vs hypoxic-ischemic) further modulated prognosis.

papers.title: Transient Sleep Deprivation Induces Persistent Auditory Neuropathy via ROS-Initiated Neuroinflammation and BK Channel Suppression.
papers.summary: This study establishes a dose-dependent association between sleep disturbance severity and hearing loss in patients, and uses a mouse model to show that acute sleep deprivation causes persistent high-frequency hearing loss via cochlear synaptopathy. The mechanism involves transient oxidative stress initiating chronic neuroinflammation that suppresses BK channels, and antioxidant or BK channel opener treatment prevents the deficits.

papers.title: Closed-loop auditory stimulation in phase with slow waves during sleep enhances cerebrospinal fluid flow in humans.
papers.summary: This study developed closed-loop auditory stimulation synchronized with slow-wave peaks during sleep and used simultaneous MRI to show that it enhances cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow waves in healthy adults. The effect was phase-dependent and accompanied by widespread hemodynamic waves, demonstrating a causal link between neural slow waves and CSF flow.

papers.title: Bidirectional EEG Neurofeedback of Sensorimotor Beta Oscillations Reveals Asymmetric Modulation and Strategy-Dependent Learning.
papers.summary: This exploratory study assessed the ability of healthy participants to bidirectionally modulate sensorimotor beta power using EEG neurofeedback in a double-blind sham-controlled within-subjects design. Thirteen participants successfully decreased beta activity, three successfully increased it, and two demonstrated bidirectional control; real neurofeedback success was significantly higher than sham when sham was first, indicating a transfer learning effect.

papers.title: Smartphone-based digital phenotyping of sighted non-24-h sleep-wake disorder: A 258-d continuous circadian monitoring study.
papers.summary: This study presents a 258-day smartphone-based digital phenotyping method for monitoring circadian rhythms in a sighted individual with Non-24-h sleep-wake disorder. The smartphone-derived circadian period (25.16 h) closely matched actigraphy (25.11 h), demonstrating its utility as a low-burden alternative for long-term circadian monitoring.

papers.title: Serial amplitude-integrated electroencephalography trajectories and brain-injury-associated functional immaturity in extremely preterm infants.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study characterized postmenstrual-age-specific Burdjalov maturation trajectories in 156 extremely preterm infants using 723 serial amplitude-integrated EEG recordings. Infants with major brain injury scored on average 1.45 points lower at 32 weeks PMA, with persistent differences across PMA windows, but the study cautions against interpreting unstable linear interactions as biological recovery.

papers.title: Prognostic assessment of comatose patients after cardiac arrest: construction of a simplified monitoring EEG risk score across different time windows.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study developed a Simplified EEG Risk Score (SERS) for prognostic assessment in 251 comatose patients after cardiac arrest. SERS incorporated EEG features such as background amplitude, dominant frequency, continuity, reactivity, and sleep elements, achieving high AUCs (0.881-0.912) across time windows and outperforming individual EEG features and clinical predictors.

papers.title: A Rapid Workflow For Modeling Sleep Deprivation-Induced Recognition Memory Deficits In Mice Using Novel Object Recognition and Hippocampal Biomarkers.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a rapid workflow for modeling sleep deprivation-induced recognition memory deficits in mice using a 5-hour gentle-handling sleep deprivation after novel object recognition training. The workflow links behavioral outcomes to hippocampal inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, emphasizing standardization and reproducibility.

papers.title: Circadian immunoregulation in cutaneous wound healing: from immune cell temporal heterogeneity to chronotherapeutic strategies.
papers.summary: This review summarizes how circadian rhythms regulate immune cell recruitment, activation, and resolution during cutaneous wound healing, focusing on neutrophil trafficking and macrophage temporal heterogeneity. It discusses how circadian disruption in conditions like diabetes, aging, and sleep disturbance may desynchronize immune responses and promote chronic wounds, and proposes chronotherapeutic strategies aligning interventions with endogenous rhythms.

papers.title: Visual Environmental Interventions and Preoperative Sleep: The Role of Curtain Color in Surgical Patients.
papers.summary: In a prospective randomized study of 190 patients undergoing elective thoracic surgery, light-colored ward curtains (beige/light blue) were associated with better preoperative sleep quality compared to dark-colored curtains, as measured by subjective questionnaires and actigraphy. Multivariable analyses indicated that curtain color remained independently associated with both subjective and objective sleep outcomes.

papers.title: A Dual Soft Attention Network for Automatic Sleep Staging via Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Signals.
papers.summary: This paper proposes SleepECGNet, a dual soft attention network for automatic sleep staging using single-lead ECG signals. The model, evaluated on HMC, MGH, and SHHS1 datasets, improved classification with expanded input timeframes and showed transferability to sleep apnea recognition using the Apnea-ECG corpus.

papers.title: Tai Chi modulates resting alpha and theta EEG rhythms in female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence during compulsory detoxification.
papers.summary: In a 6-month randomized trial with 32 female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence, both Tai Chi and routine physical rehabilitation reduced resting alpha and theta EEG power across multiple cortical regions. Acutely, Tai Chi elicited higher alpha and theta power in widespread regions compared to treadmill exercise, suggesting greater cortical relaxation and internal focus.

papers.title: The Circadian System and Chronic Kidney Disease Risk: Epidemiological Evidence.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized 34 studies examining associations between circadian rhythm determinants (shift work, artificial light at night, melatonin, chronotype, social jetlag, insomnia, sleep duration) and chronic kidney disease risk. Consistent evidence linked shift work, evening chronotype, prolonged social jetlag, and both short and long sleep duration to elevated CKD risk.

papers.title: Novel Sleep-Promoting Peptides from Sea Cucumbers Targeting the GABAa Receptor Identified by a Multitechnique Approach of Proteolysis Simulation, Molecular Docking, and Pharmacophore Modeling.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
papers.summary: Using proteolysis simulation, molecular docking, and pharmacophore modeling, the study identified two novel sleep-promoting peptides from sea cucumbers: Leu-Phe-Ala (LFA) and Thr-Phe-Trp (TFW). In PCPA-induced insomnia mice, both peptides significantly shortened sleep latency, and LFA alleviated anxiety-like behavior and ameliorated neurotransmitter imbalance.

papers.title: Heart rate fragmentation in psychiatry: across age stages and association with conventional heart rate variability.
papers.summary: In 3,813 psychiatric patients across four age groups, heart rate fragmentation (HRF) measured by the percentage of inflection points (PIP) increased with age while conventional heart rate variability indices declined. PIP showed sex differences in younger groups and limited diagnostic specificity, and was inversely associated with conventional HRV, particularly high-frequency power.

papers.title: Polysomnographic characteristics of excessive daytime sleepiness in postmenopausal women with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study in postmenopausal women with obstructive sleep apnea found that excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) was independently associated with higher respiratory disturbance index (total, supine, REM, NREM) and lower oxygen saturation. A four-variable model (RDI, REM RDI, mean and minimum oxygen saturation) had moderate discriminative ability (AUROC 0.693).

papers.title: Aquaporin-4 mis-localization decreases glymphatic clearance of α-synuclein in an alpha-syntrophin knock out mouse model and promotes α-synuclein pathology and aggregate propagation.
papers.summary: This study demonstrated that mis-localization of aquaporin-4, as seen in alpha-syntrophin knockout mice, impairs glymphatic clearance of α-synuclein and promotes α-synuclein aggregate propagation. Human post-mortem cortex also showed that α-synuclein pathology is associated with aquaporin-4 mis-localization, linking glymphatic dysfunction to synucleinopathy progression.

papers.title: The rice circadian clock orchestrates the rhizosphere microbiome to synchronize nitrogen supply with plant demand.
papers.summary: The study shows that the rice circadian clock component Nhd1 coordinates rhizosphere microbial activity with diurnal nitrogen uptake by driving rhythmic root exudation of quercetin 3-gentiobioside and baimaside, which upregulate microbial nitrogen-cycling genes. A synchronized microbial community engineered to match this diurnal nitrogen release increased grain yield and nitrogen use efficiency in field trials, with greater benefits in cultivars with weak Nhd1 alleles.

papers.title: Integrative and mind-body approaches to law enforcement professional wellness.
papers.summary: This systematic review assessed 21 studies of integrative and mind-body health interventions (mindfulness, self-regulation, wellness programs, sleep, yoga, detoxification) for US law enforcement personnel. Mindfulness generally improved mental health, burnout, and stress; yoga improved mood and perceived stress; wellness programs improved health behaviors, but results were mixed across and within intervention types.

papers.title: Moderators of the Effects of Telehealth Mindfulness-based Interventions for Chronic Pain: A Secondary Responder Analysis of the LAMP Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This secondary responder analysis of the LAMP randomized controlled trial tested moderating effects of gender and mental health diagnoses on outcomes of two telehealth mindfulness-based interventions (group and self-paced) versus usual care in 811 veterans with chronic pain. Both interventions showed higher improvement rates across all outcomes than usual care; in the group intervention, women had greater improvement in pain severity and depression than men, and those with anxiety diagnoses had less improvement in PTSD.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics profiling of insomnia-related molecular features reveals microbiome, immune, and therapy-relevant heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
papers.summary: This study integrated multi-omics data from 3,026 colorectal cancer patients to identify two insomnia-related molecular subtypes (IS1/IS2) with distinct survival, immune infiltration, and intratumoral microbiome profiles. An insomnia score (ISscore) was developed and validated, showing association with immunotherapy response indicators and stratifying survival risk.

papers.title: Circadian-Inspired Hydrogel Moisture Electricity Generation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a circadian-inspired hydrogel moisture electric generator that uses diurnal temperature-moisture fluctuations to drive reversible internal water redistribution and sustained electricity generation. The device delivered a short-circuit current density of 75 µA cm−2, open-circuit voltage of 0.4–1 V, and power density of 16 µW cm−2, maintaining performance over 57 days.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and exploratory serum biomarker findings in vestibular migraine: a cross-sectional case-control study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional case-control study characterized clinical features and explored serum biomarkers in 145 patients with vestibular migraine and 50 healthy controls. Female sex, higher BMI, and positive family history were associated with vestibular migraine; serum CGRP and GDF-15 levels were associated with case status, with exploratory AUCs of 0.794 for CGRP, 0.898 for GDF-15, and 0.927 for their combination.

papers.title: Sleep and Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
papers.summary: This review discusses the prevalence and impact of sleep disorders on disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), including functional dyspepsia and irritable bowel syndrome. It covers mechanisms linking sleep disruption to brain-gut axis dysfunction and provides practical tips for evaluating and treating patients with both conditions.

papers.title: From a Pinched Nerve to a Fatal Prognosis: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease Masquerading as Cervical Myelopathy.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 53-year-old man with sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease initially presenting with symptoms mimicking cervical myelopathy, leading to diagnostic delay and surgical intervention. Diagnosis was confirmed by positive RT-QuIC and elevated CSF tau and 14-3-3 proteins, and the patient declined to death.

papers.title: Association between circadian rhythm sleep disorders and dry eye disease: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study using real-world clinical data from 48,356 patients found that circadian rhythm sleep disorders were associated with a significantly increased risk of dry eye disease over 1, 3, and 5 years after propensity score matching. The adjusted hazard ratios ranged from 2.31 at 1 year to 2.04 at 5 years.

papers.title: Utidelone-associated chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy: an evidence-stratified narrative review of mechanisms, risk identification, and management strategies.
papers.summary: This evidence-stratified narrative review synthesizes mechanisms, risk factors, and management of utidelone-associated chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), highlighting that peripheral neuropathy occurs in 59% of patients receiving utidelone plus capecitabine (grade 3: 22%) versus 8% (grade 3: <1%) with capecitabine alone. It proposes a practical management framework and distinguishes utidelone-specific evidence from extrapolated taxane/platinum findings, noting limited direct mechanistic data except a mouse study linking allodynia to TRPA1 upregulation and oxidative stress.

papers.title: Validation of the Spinal Cord Injury Secondary Conditions Scale (SCI-SCS): Comparing self-reports with clinician ratings obtained during routine annual follow-up appointments in a specialized SCI center.
papers.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
papers.summary: This monocentric validation study assessed the psychometric properties of the SCI-Secondary Conditions Scale (SCI-SCS) in 300 patients with spinal cord injury and compared self-reports with clinician ratings obtained during routine annual follow-ups. The SCI-SCS showed good fit and unidimensionality, but significant discrepancies were found for sexual dysfunction, sleep, contractures, bladder/bowel dysfunction, and circulatory problems, with patients tending to report higher severity than clinicians.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
